newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: China's airlines boost passenger, cargo growth.
newsitem.headline: China's airlines boost passenger, cargo growth.

text.p: China's airlines flew 55.5 million passengers in 1996, up 8.5 percent over a year ago, while air cargo traffic grew more than 13 percent to 1.14 million tonnes, a senior aviation official said on Friday.

Hai Liancheng, finance chief at China's Civil Aviation Administration (CAAC) also told a Geneva international aviation conference that air freight turnover rose on a tonne-km basis to 8.1 billion tonne-km in 1996, up 12.7 percent.
The total turnover on a tonne-km basis now put China in the 11th place in the world, he added.
China's aviation industry is expanding rapidly and its planes are now flying to 797 routes, of which 694 are domestic, said Liancheng.

Airline industry officials say that on a worldwide scale, China has a long way to go to catch up with the United States, Western European countries and Japan in terms of air passenger and cargo traffic.

By comparison, the world's busiest cargo airport Memphis, base of U.S. express freight carrier Federal Express, handled 167,015 tonnes of cargo in November 1996 alone, according to the Geneva-based Airports Council International (ACI).

Air cargo traffic handled by 473 airports around the world totalled 4.4 million tonnes in November, led by North America, the biggest of ACI's six cargo-handling regions, which reported 2.26 million tonnes of cargo traffic.

China's passenger traffic of 55.5 million travellers for the whole of 1996 compared to total world traffic of 189.3 million flyers alone in November, including Europe airports which handled 52.9 million travellers.
Liancheng said Chinese planes were now serving 85 international routes including 53 cities in 33 countries -- 38 cities and 19 countries more than the level in 1990.
By 2010, China expected to boost its air passenger traffic to 100 million travellers and cargo traffic to two million tonnes, both up by nearly 100 percent over 1995 levels, he said.
Long-term plans also foresaw an air freight turnover of 14 billion tonne-km, he added.
